reason: The hypothesis makes specific claims about copper segregation, surface premelting, and inward propagation in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles, but no prior evidence is cited to support any of these key premises. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover the segregation behavior or melting mechanism in this specific high-entropy alloy nanoparticle system.
premises: Copper segregates to the surface of FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles at high temperatures
Surface copper segregation creates a low-melting-point surface layer
This surface layer initiates premelting at the nanoparticle surface
Melting then propagates inward from the surface to the core
Suppressing copper segregation will delay premelting onset and raise the effective melting temperature
